chunks: Al-Kafi: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was seated in the study-circle of Rabia al-Rayy, when a bedouin came and asked Rabia al-Rayy about a matter, and he answered him. When he fell silent, the bedouin said to him: 'Is it upon your neck?' Rabia remained silent and did not reply to him with anything. He repeated the question to him, and he answered him in the same way. The bedouin said to him again: 'Is it upon your neck?' Rabia remained silent. Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'It is upon his neck.' He said: 'Did he not say: And every giver of Fatwa is liable?'

key_terms.رَبِيعَ الرَّأْيِ: Rabia al-Rayy, a prominent early jurist
key_terms.مُفْتٍ: Jurist or one who issues Fatwa

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the liability of a jurist who issues a Fatwa without sufficient knowledge?
ai.summary: This narrative from al-Kafi illustrates the principle of liability for those who issue legal opinions (Fatwa). When a bedouin asked Rabia al-Rayy a question and Rabia answered, the bedouin asked if the answer was 'upon his neck' (i.e., is he responsible for it). Rabia remained silent, indicating acceptance of responsibility. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarified that the answer is indeed upon Rabia's neck, citing the general rule that every jurist issuing a Fatwa is liable for its correctness.
